title: Lucky Thompson quits and Dexter Gordon comes in; route to Boston
summary: Lucky leaves in Boston because he cannot stand the band's behavior, and Dexter Gordon replaces him.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: But anyway, to get ahead of the story a little... About Lucky Thompson. Later we played Boston, Massachusetts, and Lucky just went to Billy Eckstine and told him, "Look, I've had enough of this. I can't stand it any more. These guys are doing everything" and so-and-so-and-so. So Lucky quit the band. And that was when they sent and got Dexter Gordon.

After we played Cincinnati, where Gene Ammons joined us, we went to Chicago and we played, I think, the Regal Theatre. Then I think after that we played either Pittsburgh or Detroit -- I don't remember. But then we went to Boston and we played Boston in this old club up there that all the big bands used to broadcast. We might have been one of the last big bands to go in there. I can't remember the name of the club right now, but it was quite a famous club back in the Thirties [THE SOUTHLAND?]. Because I used to hear broadcasts from there back early in the Thirties, with big bands.
